## Key Insights

1. Summer Sowing Status: As on May 09, 2025, the area sown under the Summer crops is 78.82 lakh ha as compared to 71.94 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year.  Of this, area  of  32.02  lakh  ha  has  been  sown  under  rice  this  year  against  the  previous  year  area  of 28.57 lakh ha (increase of 3.44 lakh ha).
2. Rabi  harvesting  Status:  As  on  09.05.2025,  98.34%  of  Rabi  sown  area  has  been  harvested  all over  India.  Approximately  100.00%  area  of  Pulses  has  been  harvested;  94.60%  area  of  Shri Anna  &  Coarse  Cereals  mainly  in  Jowar  (99.66%);  99.89  %  area  of  Oilseeds  majorly  in Rapeseed & Mustard (100.00%) & Groundnut (98.56%); 100.00% of Wheat and 81.56% area of Rice has been harvested for Rabi crops 2024-25.
3. Rabi Season Area Coverage : For Rabi horticulture crops ,  major producing states report the following sowing areas: Onion - 12.58 lakh ha (9.76 lakh ha last year), Potato - 20.03 lakh ha (19.56 lakh ha last year), Tomato - 3.29 lakh ha (3.14 lakh ha last year).

## 4. Weather Update :

- a) Temperature: Gradual rise in maximum temperatures by 3-5°C likely over Northwest India, by 2-3°C likely over Central India and Gujarat State during next 7 days.  No significant change in maximum temperatures likely over interior Maharashtra during next 2 days and gradual rise by 2-4°C thereafter for subsequent 5 days.  No significant change in maximum temperatures likely over rest parts of the country.
- b) Rainfall Distribution: From Mar 01- 13 May, 2025, the All-India cumulative rainfall is 5% lower than its Long Period Average (LPA), with regional variations: (i) East & Northeast India: -28%; (ii) Northwest India: -21%; (iii) Central India: 90%; and South Peninsula: 35%.

Fairly  widespread  to  scattered,  light  to  moderate  rainfall  accompanied  with  isolated thunderstorm activity observed in some parts southern Peninsula, east and northeast India during the week; due to  north-south and east-west lower level wind convergence over the region.

Rainfall  accompanied  with  thunderstorms  and  lightning  likely  to  continue  over  West, Central & South Peninsular India till 16 th  May, 2025.

Heavy  to  very  heavy  rainfall  accompanied  with  thunderstorms  &  lightning  likely  over Northeast India during next 5 days.

Overall,  above  normal  rainfall  along  with  thunderstorm  &  lightening  are  likely  over Central and South Peninsular India; normal to above normal over many parts of east & northeast India and below normal over many parts of northwest India during the week.

## Inputs Situation

- a) Water Reservoir Status : As on 08 th  May 2025, the total live water storage in 161 important reservoirs across the country (monitored by CWC) is 57.97 Billion Cubic Meter, which is 32% of total live storage capacity (182.44 BCM).The current year's storage is nearly 118 percent of last year's storage and 116 percent of the average storage of the last ten years during  the  corresponding  period.  The  overall  storage  position  is  better than  the corresponding period of last year in the country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period.
- b) Groundwater Levels : Approximately 66.6% of monitoring wells show water levels between 0-5 m, while 29.1% report levels between 5-10 m. Decadal analysis (2014-2023) indicates a rise in 64.9% of wells and a decline in 35.1% as of August 2024.
- c) Seeds  and  Fertilizers :  For  Rabi  2024-25,  certified  seed  availability  is  337.98  lakh  quintals against a requirement of 307.07 lakh quintals, ensuring a surplus of 30.90 lakh quintals. The fertilizer supply remains stable across all products.
6. Pests & Diseases: The overall intensity of pests and diseases remained below the Economic Threshold Level.

## Week 1 (09 May - 15 May):

-  Oilseeds: About 9.51  lakh ha area coverage has been reported compared to 9.23 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year.

Key Insights

1. Summer Sowing Status: As on May 09, 2025, the area sown under the Summer crops is 78.82 lakh ha as compared to 71.94 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year.  Of this, area  of  32.02  lakh  ha  has  been  sown  under  rice  this  year  against  the  previous  year  area  of 28.57 lakh ha (increase of 3.44 lakh ha).

4. Weather Update :

- a) Temperature: Gradual rise in maximum temperatures by 3-5°C likely over Northwest India, by 2-3°C likely over Central India and Gujarat State during next 7 days.  No significant change in maximum temperatures likely over interior Maharashtra during next 2 days and gradual rise by 2-4°C thereafter for subsequent 5 days.  No significant change in maximum temperatures likely over rest parts of the country.
- b) Rainfall Distribution: From Mar 01- 13 May, 2025, the All-India cumulative rainfall is 5% lower than its Long Period Average (LPA), with regional variations: (i) East & Northeast India: -28%; (ii) Northwest India: -21%; (iii) Central India: 90%; and South Peninsula: 35%.

Fairly  widespread  to  scattered,  light  to  moderate  rainfall  accompanied  with  isolated thunderstorm activity observed in some parts southern Peninsula, east and northeast India during the week; due to  north-south and east-west lower level wind convergence over the region.

Rainfall  accompanied  with  thunderstorms  and  lightning  likely  to  continue  over  West, Central & South Peninsular India till 16 th  May, 2025.

Heavy  to  very  heavy  rainfall  accompanied  with  thunderstorms  &  lightning  likely  over Northeast India during next 5 days.

Overall,  above  normal  rainfall  along  with  thunderstorm  &  lightening  are  likely  over Central and South Peninsular India; normal to above normal over many parts of east & northeast India and below normal over many parts of northwest India during the week.
